item.title: Interesting Concept, but Meh
item.content:encoded: I like the idea of "stars in your eyes" being taken literally; but the article doesn't go anywhere with that so we have an autistic blind girl with strange eyes…it's…there's not enough there for an upvote. Something creepy or wrong happening because of the motions of her eyes or IDK, it needs something. -1 from me.

item.title: Re: Poor kid.
item.content:encoded:
One suggestion: Since the child is Japanese, perhaps a Japanese name would be more fitting instead of "Stella"?

The Japanese have a lot of loanwords from other languages, including Castella, which I always thought was cute.

I personally feel like the current name is fine.

item.title: Poor kid.
item.content:encoded:
Upvoted. The part where she's not allowed a name and only her SCP designation is so sad. It really humanizes her and shows how cold the foundation really is.

One suggestion: Since the child is Japanese, perhaps a Japanese name would be more fitting instead of "Stella"? "Hoshi" means "star" in Japanese, and Hoshiko means "star child". Just a thought.

item.content:encoded:
In my headcanon (and one of the many, many tale ideas I don't know if I'll ever get to), Stella ends up becoming unlikely best friends with SCP-2118.

2118 and 134 meet. At first, 2118 tries signing with 134, but is then told that 134 is blind. The two of them sit quietly for a long time, until 2118 works up the courage to turn to 134 and say, "I like your eyes."

134 gives the faintest of smiles and replies, "I like your voice."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Pretty conflicted about this one. I like the concept, and the fact that the stars in her eyes don't match up to any known constellations definitely has some interesting implications. I'm also a bit ashamed to admit that I kinda enjoy the Series I-ness of the article, what with the "severe reprimanding" of people who call her Stella, the questionable redaction, etc. Something about it feels… nostalgic? Kinda like minor glitches on an NES game. It's reminding me of what I saw when I first discovered the site, and that's petty cool. But Series I issues are still issues nonetheless, and they don't do the article much good besides the nostalgia factor. Tentative upvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This one's still really interesting, but it's showing its age. Specifically, there's absolutely no reason why she can't be referred to as Stella in her presence. It would make her comfortable, which would reduce the chances of an escape or manifestation of some weird new aspect of her condition in anger (what if she can shoot supernovas out of her eyes or something? They don't know.) That portion of the article feels left over from an era when we assumed the Foundation was just filled with dickholes. I'd reccommend either providing a better reason why it's forbidden, removing it from the article, or just putting in her containment procedures that she should be referred to as Stella in interaction and SCP-134 in official documentation.

It's kind of loosely held together at first, but it just falls apart when it gets to the good part (actually describing the anomaly and not just the kid). I want to revisit this, but I think I'll leave my downvote for now.
